authority: Candidate advantages and verification plans; they do not establish performance or market conclusions

items.title: Compactness and the first playable experience
items.claim: On-demand modules, target resources, and loading strategies may establish advantages in initial packages and first interaction.
items.measure: Measure empty release packages, functional packages, total resources, cold-start download/decoding/initialization/upload, and time to the first effective action separately.

items.title: Sustained complex-UI frame times
items.claim: Phased invalidation, layout isolation, virtualization, and order-preserving execution may improve complex-UI tail frame times.
items.measure: Combine unchanged, sparsely invalidated, fully invalidated, and interactive workloads; record layout/preparation/GC/CPU/GPU, P95/P99, input latency, and visual correctness.

items.title: Power consumption and heat
items.claim: Budgeted scheduling, uploads, fill, and quality control may improve sustained energy consumption and thermal stability.
items.measure: Use identical content and conditions for 20 to 30 minutes; record power/temperature rise/throttling/frame times, separating estimates from measurements.

items.title: Mixed 2D and 3D efficiency
items.claim: Separate execution lists, shared resources, and frame scheduling may support both 3D scenes and complex 2D presentation.
items.measure: Use identical assets/quality for character scenes, transparent effects, UI, 2D skeletons, and frame sequences; check CPU/GPU, overdraw, uploads, memory, and animation events.

items.title: Reliability of continuous AI creation
items.claim: Unified project semantics, diagnostics, and recovery may improve success rates for new AI creators making continuous changes and deliveries.
items.measure: Measure first playable results, multi-round modification success, preservation of unrelated gameplay, undo, human takeover, time, and cost, grouped by creator experience.

items.title: Minimal-intervention migration and consistency
items.claim: Deterministic conversion plus Agent repairs and old/new comparisons may complete migration with little intervention within declared supported scope.
items.measure: Group by project version/dependencies; count success over all samples, manual interventions/time, AI cost, and old/new behavior/visual/platform comparisons, without excluding failed samples.

items.title: Iteration cost of stable interfaces
items.claim: Versioned contracts and replaceable internal implementations may reduce costs of backend replacement, host updates, and legacy-work upgrades.
items.measure: Measure change scope before/after upgrades, migration counts, regression failures, repair effort, and the proportion of works still executable.

items.title: Compilation/debug waits and AI-edit feedback
items.claim: Stable native TS compilers, separated preview/checking, and content-based incremental builds may shorten modification feedback in complete creation workflows.
items.measure: Fix representative projects/hardware and caches; separately measure cold preview, warm edit-to-frame, type diagnostics, resource shader conversion, and target publication, including error localization and continuous-edit success.
